comparison: Both support the data collection and marker identification methodology (C3, C46, C49, C54-C56, C179-C180). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of specific claims, while peer reviewers offer broader endorsement of the 'rigorous methodologies' and 'thorough reference dataset collections.'

Both support the marker peak identification process (C50, C57-C64). OpenEval validates the multi-step differential analysis approach with specific evidence, while peer reviewers affirm the overall quality without detailed critique of individual steps.

Both support the PCA analysis and clustering validation (C66-C69). OpenEval provides quantitative assessment of silhouette coefficients and batch effects, while peer reviewers accept the characterization without specific technical concerns.

Both support cell-type specificity validation (C71-C76). OpenEval details evidence from multiple figures showing specificity and genomic location analysis, while peer reviewers implicitly accept through overall positive evaluation of marker quality.

Both support the annotation and enrichment analyses (C77-C81, C83). OpenEval validates the use of multiple databases and biological property capture, while peer reviewers accept the biological relevance of markers without specific critique.

Both support the EPIC-ATAC framework integration (C4, C47, C53, C84-C96). OpenEval validates specific methodological choices including TPM-like transformation, while peer reviewers praise the 'rigorous methodologies' and tool quality broadly.

Both support experimental validation on true bulk samples (C5, C48, C98-C105). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative assessment of correlation/RMSE values and outlier analysis, while peer reviewers describe 'simple and understandable experiments' demonstrating accuracy.

Both support pseudobulk validation (C106-C107). OpenEval validates high correlation and low RMSE on multiple scATAC-Seq datasets, while peer reviewers affirm the 'robust estimates' and 'convincing' validation results.

Both support the benchmarking methodology and results (C108-C115). OpenEval validates the comparison approach and broad applicability findings, while peer reviewers acknowledge 'robust benchmarking endeavours' against multiple datasets and tools.

Both support cancer sample validation and uncharacterized cell prediction (C116-C123). OpenEval validates the methodology and interpretation with appropriate caveats, while peer reviewers affirm the tool 'successfully predicts accurate proportions' in tumor samples.

Both support benchmarking on cancer datasets showing EPIC-ATAC superiority (C124-C133). OpenEval validates performance metrics and methodological distinctions, while peer reviewers confirm 'EPIC-ATAC seems to perform well in benchmarking analyses.'

Both address the absolute vs. relative fraction distinction and two-benchmark approach (C127-C133). OpenEval validates this methodological consideration, while peer reviewers accept the 'detailed' description of settings for robust comparison.

Both support cell-type-specific performance analysis and acknowledge limitations for low-abundance cells (C135-C141, C199-C202). OpenEval provides detailed correlation/RMSE analysis, while peer reviewers treat these as honest assessments rather than fundamental flaws.

Both support T-cell subtype analysis and accept decreased performance for closely related subtypes (C142-C149). OpenEval validates the limitation with empirical evidence, while peer reviewers accept this as an expected limitation rather than a failure.

Both strongly support the breast cancer cohort application (C6, C150-C162). OpenEval validates correlation with original study metrics and additional findings, while peer reviewers explicitly state the 'application results on breast cancer tumor tissues are convincing.'

Both support the modality comparison analysis (C163-C171). OpenEval validates the methodology and performance comparison, while peer reviewers note the demonstration that 'both modalities led to similar performances and that they could complement each other.'

Both support matched bulk data analysis showing complementarity (C172-C178). OpenEval validates cell-type-specific differences and moderate improvement from averaging, while peer reviewers view this as strengthening the EPIC-ATAC approach.

Both support the uncharacterized cell prediction capability (C186, C188). OpenEval validates this as a key distinguishing feature with appropriate caveats, while peer reviewers affirm the tool 'advances existing methods' through comprehensive reference profiles.

Both support the honest assessment of accuracy and limitations (C199-C202). OpenEval validates the 8% average error as consistent with RNA-Seq methods, while peer reviewers accept these limitations as part of 'very high quality' work.

Both support the T-cell subtype limitation and recommendation (C203-C205). OpenEval validates this with empirical evidence, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the recommendation to use major cell-type populations as reasonable.

Both support the finding of similar performance between ATAC-Seq and RNA-Seq modalities (C208). OpenEval validates this with pseudobulk and bulk PBMC analyses, while peer reviewers accept the complementarity finding.

Both support the main contributions summary (C220-C222). OpenEval validates these as accurate summaries of major findings, while peer reviewers affirm the overall quality and rigor of the methodology and results.
Peer reviewers accept computational efficiency (C134) without comment, indicating implicit acceptance. No corresponding detailed OpenEval assessment of computational requirements was found.
